My vote is for B. While both solutions implement a 2D flight simulator with intentional bugs, Solution B is more concise, easier to understand, and has a cleaner structure. It separates the simulation logic from the rendering, making it more modular and maintainable. The use of delta time for updating the aircraft state also results in more consistent and realistic simulation.

Solution A, while providing a more comprehensive set of features and bug demonstrations, is more cluttered and less readable. The use of global variables and extensive use of bug flags can make the code harder to follow and debug.

In summary, while both solutions demonstrate an understanding of the flight simulation domain and intentional bug introduction, Solution B wins due to its superior code organization, readability, and performance characteristics.
